record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
record.original_question: Classify all recurrent one-sided and two-sided sequences over a finite alphabet whose maximal pattern complexity satisfies p*(n)=2n for every n≥1; equivalently, determine all one-sided and two-sided pattern Sturmian sequences.

evidence.quote: The sequence x is pattern Sturmian if p∗(n) = 2n for all n ≥ 1. Note that a Sturmian sequence is necessarily pattern Sturmian. The converse inclusion, however, does not hold. Problem 2.1.1 Determine all single sided (resp. double sided) sequences that are pattern Sturmian.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $x = (x_n)$ be an infinite sequence over $A$, either one-sided ($n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$) or two-sided ($n \in \mathbb{Z}$). For an integer $k \ge 1$ and a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative integers $\tau = (\tau(0), \tau(1), \ldots, \tau(k-1))$ with $\tau(0) = 0$, define the $\tau$-pattern set of $x$ as
\[
F_\tau(x) = \{(x_{n+\tau(0)}, x_{n+\tau(1)}, \ldots, x_{n+\tau(k-1)}) : n \text{ in the index set of } x\}.
\]
The maximal pattern complexity of $x$ is
\[
p^*_x(k) = \sup_{\tau} \#F_\tau(x),
\]
where the supremum is over all such $\tau$ of length $k$. The sequence $x$ is called recurrent if every finite factor occurring in $x$ occurs infinitely often (in both directions, in the two-sided case). Call $x$ pattern Sturmian if $p^*_x(n) = 2n$ for all $n \ge 1$.

Classify (up to relabeling of the alphabet) all recurrent one-sided infinite sequences and all recurrent two-sided infinite sequences over a finite alphabet that are pattern Sturmian; equivalently, give an explicit structural description of every such sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification problem for pattern Sturmian sequences (those with maximal pattern complexity p*(n) = 2n for all n) was raised by Kamae and collaborators; partial results characterize the language structure of pattern Sturmian words and show Sturmian words form a strict subclass, but no complete classification of one-sided or two-sided pattern Sturmian sequences appears in the literature. The problem is listed as an open problem in surveys on mathematical quasicrystals, and no resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Language structure of pattern Sturmian words (Kamae, Rao, Tan, Xue)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the language structure of pattern Sturmian words; partial structural results, not a full classification.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial structural results are known about pattern Sturmian words.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and conjectures in the theory of mathematical quasicrystals
status_evidence.snippet: Problem: Determine all single sided (resp. double sided) sequences that are pattern Sturmian.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of pattern Sturmian sequences is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Three complexity functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses maximal pattern complexity and pattern Sturmian words; notes Sturmian words are not the only ones with p*(n)=2n.
status_evidence.claim: The class of sequences with p*(n)=2n strictly contains Sturmian sequences and lacks a complete classification.
